observations: Photo 0 shows the right side of a dark smartphone held in a hand; side button, volume keys, and SIM tray are visible, but no screen, back, or branding.
Photo 1 shows a similar side view with the bottom edge partly visible; no model marking is readable.
Photo 2 shows the bottom edge with a charging port and speaker and microphone holes; no branding or model identifier appears.
All three photos carry a HUSHGADGETS LIMITED watermark.

claims.evidence: No model name or storage capacity is visible on the phone in photos 0-2.
The screen is not shown powered on; only exterior edges are visible.
The front screen and rear casing are not shown in any photo.
eSIM capability cannot be determined from exterior photos.
Pickup availability cannot be confirmed from photos.

risks.risk: The phone is not an iPhone 16 Pro or is a counterfeit device.
risks.proof: Photo of the rear casing with Apple logo and model text, or a settings About screen.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unverified generic smartphone rather than an iPhone 16 Pro.

risks.proof: Screenshot of Settings showing total capacity.
risks.if_unproven: priced as lower or unknown storage.

risks.risk: The phone does not power on or has hidden functional faults.
risks.proof: Video of the phone booting, responding to touch, and making a call.

risks.risk: The front or back glass is cracked.
risks.proof: Clear front and rear photographs of the device.

risks.risk: The eSIM is inactive or the device is carrier locked.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the eSIM or cellular settings menu.

proof_requests: Photo of the back of the phone showing branding and model text.
Screenshot of Settings > General > About showing model, capacity, and serial number.
Video of the phone powering on, unlocking, and making a call.
Front and rear photos to confirm there are no cracks.
response.reason: The photos show only the side and bottom of a smartphone with no readable brand or model, so the seller's iPhone 16 Pro claim cannot be confirmed and the price-setting model is missing.
